bull.b: Strong revenue growth alongside higher traffic indicates broad customer demand rather than expansion alone. Sustained comparable-sales momentum can support operating leverage, reinforce brand relevance, and provide a durable base for continued unit growth over the next several quarters.

High new-unit productivity and attractive average unit volume support a scalable restaurant model. Continued openings can expand the revenue base while allowing CAVA to leverage its brand, operating systems, and site-level economics across a larger national footprint.

Substantial liquidity and positive operating cash flow give CAVA flexibility to fund restaurant expansion, absorb cost variability, and support strategic investments without immediate reliance on external financing. This financial capacity strengthens resilience as the business scales.

bear.b: Rising food, labor, and delivery-related costs are pressuring restaurant economics even while sales grow. If these expenses remain elevated, they could limit operating leverage, reduce cash generation, and make reported profitability more sensitive to execution and pricing.

The decline from unusually strong 2024 profitability shows that earnings margins have not yet demonstrated consistent durability. Lower current margins leave less protection against cost inflation or slower sales, potentially constraining reinvestment and earnings growth.

Increasing debt reduces financial flexibility if operating trends soften, while modest free-cash-flow conversion indicates substantial capital needs remain. Together, these factors may constrain discretionary capital allocation and increase dependence on sustained operating performance.
